name: Tjeldsund Bridge
facts: The Tjeldsund Bridge, a 1,007‑metre suspension road, opened on 22 August 1967 when King Olav V crossed its 290‑metre main span, marking a milestone in Norway's postwar infrastructure boom.
Constructed over 30 months, the bridge demanded 375,000 work hours, 112,000 bags of cement, 1,200 tons of steel, and a 45‑million‑kroner investment, showcasing remarkable engineering coordination.
With a maximum sea clearance of 41 metres, the Tjeldsund Bridge allows large vessels to pass beneath, while its 32 spans elegantly distribute the load across the Tjeldsundet strait.
